title: Stakeholder Summary (One-Pager)
description: The one-page write-up that gets read instead of the 30-slide deck that doesn't. The structure forces the analyst to lead with the decision, not the methodology. Methodology lives in an appendix; the first page is for the stakeholder. The discipline is being willing to compress your three weeks of work into five sentences a CFO will read on the train.

# [Analysis title]
_For: [primary reader] · prepared by: [DA] · [date]_

## The headline (one sentence)
_What did we find. Specific. Quantified. No 'broadly speaking' or 'tends to'._

## What it means (two to three sentences)
_Why the headline matters. What decision it supports. The 'so what'._

## What we'd recommend (three bullets max)
_The action(s) the decision-maker would take. Phrased as decisions, not analyses ('approve the partner-channel investment' beats 'consider further investigation of partner-channel ROI')._

## What we're not certain about (one to three caveats)
_The honest caveats. Not hedging the headline; naming the specific things that could change the picture._

## How we got here (one paragraph)
_The methodology, plain English, one paragraph. Detailed methodology in the appendix._

## Appendix
_Full methodology, SQL, statistical detail. Linked from the one-pager; not embedded in it._

worked_examples.title: Simplified-onboarding churn finding — one-pager for the executive committee
worked_examples.content_md:
# Simplified Onboarding Is Driving 2.2× Higher Churn
_For: Executive Committee · prepared by: [DA] · 22 April 2026_

## The headline

Customers who went through the simplified onboarding (launched September 2025) are churning at **2.2× the rate** of customers from the equivalent legacy onboarding (19.2% vs 8.7% over a comparable 90-day observation window). The effect is consistent across segment, channel, and signup-month slices.

## What it means

The primary investment from last year's Q3 strategy is producing the opposite outcome to the intended one. Churn losses attributable to the simplified-onboarding cohort are roughly **£640k of annualised revenue** versus the counterfactual at the legacy rate. The CS team's escalation volume on this cohort is also 1.8× — suggesting the new onboarding is creating frustrated customers who churn rather than activated customers who stick.

## What we'd recommend

- **Pause new enrolment into the simplified onboarding for the top-12 segment by 1 May.** Default new top-12 signups back into the legacy onboarding path while we diagnose.
- **Commission a 4-week qualitative study with 8-10 churned customers** from the simplified-onboarding cohort to understand the specific drop-off moment.
- **Schedule a 30-day decision point** to either (a) reinstate simplified onboarding with fixes, (b) extend the legacy-only policy to all segments, or (c) ship a v2 of the simplified onboarding.

## What we're not certain about

- The mobile-signup observation window has a known 14% data gap (see DQ Report v0.1). The 2.2× holds across the available data but may shift slightly with full data.
- The pricing change in February affected both cohorts; we've controlled for it in the segmentation, but a small residual confound remains.
- We have not yet isolated which step in the simplified onboarding is the dropping-off point; recommendation (2) above is intended to surface that.

## How we got here

We defined cohorts based on signup date and channel: 'new_onboarding' for direct + inbound signups from 15 September 2025 onwards; 'legacy_onboarding' for the same channels prior, plus all partner-channel signups (which kept the old flow). We measured days-to-churn from signup, with consistent 90-day observation windows to avoid right-censoring bias. The 2.2× ratio was checked across three segmentation cuts (segment, channel, signup month) and held in each.

## Appendix

Full SQL: see `analyses/2026-04-churn-by-onboarding-cohort.sql`. Cohort definitions, observation-window logic, and segmentation cuts documented inline. Statistical significance: difference is significant at p<0.001 by two-sample test; the confidence interval on the ratio is [2.04, 2.39].

annotations.note: The headline does the headline's job in one sentence. 'Customers who went through the simplified onboarding are churning at 2.2× the rate' is specific, quantified, and unambiguous. 'There may be concerns with simplified onboarding adoption' is the rookie version — true and useless.
What-it-means translates the finding into business stakes. £640k of annualised revenue, 1.8× CS escalations. Numbers force the reader to engage with the consequence, not just the finding.

Recommendations as decisions, not as further analyses. 'Pause new enrolment for top-12 by 1 May' is a decision the executive committee can take. 'Consider further investigation' is the kind of recommendation that delays decisions indefinitely.
Caveats listed honestly. The 14% mobile data gap is the kind of thing that, if hidden, will surface later and undermine the finding. Surfacing it in the one-pager makes the analysis trustworthy.
Methodology in one paragraph. Plain English. The CFO does not need to read about your CTE structure on page one. If she wants the SQL, she'll click the appendix link.

common_mistakes: Leading with methodology. 'We pulled data from the signups table, joined on the events table, and segmented by…' loses the reader by line three. Lead with the finding.
Hedged headlines. 'There may be some patterns suggesting…' is not a finding; it's a fear of being wrong. Be specific or don't write the document.
Recommendations phrased as 'consider further analysis'. Make a call. The DA's job is to surface decisions, not perpetually defer them.
Caveats either omitted entirely (overclaiming) or listed exhaustively (underclaiming). Three caveats. The ones that genuinely could change the picture.
Methodology paragraph that runs to half a page. Compress. The appendix exists for a reason.
Document that's two pages. It's a one-pager. Cut.
variant_patterns: Single-stakeholder variant (writing for one named reader): tone shifts slightly to address them directly. 'Bilqis — what we found:' is acceptable in this variant.
Decision-required-now variant (the analysis is timely and a decision must follow): §3 (recommendation) becomes a single, named option with rationale, not three options to choose between.

Negative-finding variant (the analysis says 'nothing here'): the headline becomes 'no evidence that X drives Y over the observation window' — and the recommendation includes whether to commission further work or close the question.
